text.p: Bonds ended off their lows as international markets recovered some poise after sliding initially on Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's warning that inflation remained a concern.
"We closed down with the Greenspan remarks but off the lows and without widening the spreads against the (German) Bunds," said one fixed-income trader.
"The same is expected tomorrow," he added, refering to the spread with the German market.

The market was likely to be helped by the recovery of the escudo which followed the U.S. dollar in gaining on the mark. The Portuguese currency closed at 100.39/42 to the mark against its opening 100.43/48.
"The (bond) market closed lower but it seems to have found some sort of support at present levels despite the continuing nervousness," added another trader.
One chartist said that there was technical support for the futures contract at 107.75 with resistance at 108.50.
